text:
Maya (acme): Hey team — our app started getting 429s during the monthly refill window. UI showed 0 credits ~2026-03-01 00:04 UTC but billing shows full monthly allotment. We didn’t change anything. Anyone seen this?

Maya (acme): curl response header excerpt: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_01F8AAZ
x-quota-remaining: 0
x-quota-next-refill: 1709250000
```

Ava (support): Sorry you're seeing that, Maya — we're looking. Can you paste org id and whether you changed plan around the refill time? Also any service logs or the `x-request-id` from a failing call helps.

Maya (acme): Org: acme-org-773. We switched from Starter->Pro about 2 hours before refill (approx 2026-02-28 22:00 UTC). Streaming jobs were running during the upgrade. x-request-id from a failing call above is `req_01F8AAZ`.

Ava (support): thanks — sending to eng, will ask for quick diagnostic. Can you run this (one-off) and paste output?
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/acme-org-773/quota
```

Maya (acme): output: 
```
{"visible_credits":0,"ledger_balance":500000,"next_refill":1709250000}
```

Ava (support): Interesting — ledger_balance shows full bucket but visible_credits is 0. That suggests edge cache and ledger got out of sync. Escalating to @Ravi (eng) with the request id & timestamps.

Ravi (eng): looking. Thanks @Ava. I pulled the `req_01F8AAZ` trace — it hit edge node eu-west-2a and returned 429 because edge cache `available_tokens` flag was zero at checktime. I'll check backfill/reconciliation jobs.

Ravi (eng): Quick theory: customer did a plan upgrade pre-reset. Our proration batch ran near midnight and created a credit adjustment that lands in the billing ledger under a `prepaid` bucket. The refill job runs and marks `ledger_balance` but cache invalidation for the edge nodes is async. Meanwhile a long-lived streaming connection kept consuming tokens (client-side retries), and the edge evaluated quota from its stale cache and returned 429. So visible_credits stayed zero on edge until invalidation.

Maya (acme): So you mean money/credits exist but API still 429s? That's what we saw. Any workaround to unblock right away?

Ravi (eng): Two mitigations: 1) rotate the API key — that forces a cache refresh for that tenant on the edge layer, or 2) call our admin refresh endpoint (support-provisioned) we can run for you. I'll kick an invalidation for your org now.

QuotaBot: Invalidation job queued for org acme-org-773 (job id inval_20260301_0006).

Ravi (eng): I also saw an error in the proration runner logs where post-upgrade adjustments were written to `prepaid` ledger partition without emitting an immediate cache invalidation event when the upgrade coincided with the refill window. We're patching the runner to emit invalidations synchronously for that window.

Ava (support): Running the admin refresh for you now — will confirm when edge shows credits.

Ava (support): admin refresh done. Can you retry an API call?

Maya (acme): retrying... call succeeded, headers now: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: req_01F8BBP
x-quota-remaining: 499800
```

Maya (acme): Nice, we're back. Any ETA on full fix so this doesn’t recur for other customers?

Ravi (eng): Patch to proration runner is in review — will be deployed to prod in the next deploy window (ETA ~6 hours). Also adding an alert for mismatched `ledger_balance` vs `visible_credits` around refill windows so we can auto-invalidate faster.

Ravi (eng): As a gesture, I’ve asked billing to credit your account 2% of the monthly allotment to cover any lost requests during the outage.

Maya (acme): Thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround and the credit.

Ava (support): Sorry again for the disruption. If you see anything odd after the patch, ping us and we’ll dig deeper. :thumbsup:
